newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Skanska expects improved results in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Skanska expects improved results in 1997.

text.p: Swedish construction company Skanska said on Thursday it expected to see improved results in both its industrial and international operations this year.

"I think... we now have a good base to achieve a significant improvement in the results from our industrial operations in the coming year," managing director Melker Schorling said in the company's annual report.
He also said the results of the company's international operations would improve as would its profit margins.
"In 1996 the results and margins were relatively unchanged but the underlying trend in our results is still positive," Schorling said.
"Our U.S. operations have had good order intake in the first months of 1997."
For 1996 Skanska posted a profit after financial items of 5.17 billion crowns against 2.57 billion crowns in 1995 with order bookings rising 19 percent to 52.5 billion crowns.
